solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Starter cheers athletes, nearly all passing early leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so each following word gives up only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A race report: the crowd cheers as nearly all the athletes overtake the early front runners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' is the selector applying to every word from 'cheers' to 'early', including 'early' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury served before a meal, so it is an appetiser or starter.

indicators.note: a confused set of letters is muddled up and must be put in a new order
only half of the surname is wanted, so its back three letters are dropped

parts.note: the actor's surname, of which only the first half is kept

explanation.surface: The film star Tony Curtis is half confused, in a muddled state.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole first name joins the first half of Curtis (CUR) before the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: State in the political sense is a nation, which is what a country is: a synonym.

clue.text: You're welcome to express pleasure holding investigation about Michael Foot

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the investigation word wraps around the letter from the name

parts.note: the sound of enjoying food, as in 'nom nom'

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the pleasure word grips everything that follows it
the foot of a word is its bottom end, so only the final letter of the name is used

parts.note: the foot or last letter of Michael

explanation.surface: An invitation to be pleased about some inquiry into Michael Foot, the former Labour Party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led Britain's Labour Party; here 'Foot' just picks the last letter. 'Nom nom' is informal for relishing food.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual replies to thanks, telling someone the favour was no trouble: an idiomatic equivalent.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a person who carries luggage

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a drinks crate or delivery van; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark brown beer brewed from roasted malt, and also a hotel or station employee who carries bags.

clue.text: Servant bound to be set back for country's balance

indicators.note: set back suggests moving backwards, so the joined words are read from end to start

parts.note: a page is a boy servant
to dart is to dash or bound

explanation.surface: A servant destined to suffer a setback, for the sake of national balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'destined' but is a verb meaning leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap is the shortfall when a nation's imports exceed its exports, a figure in its balance of payments.

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborate or decorated, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Being fancy-free, unattached and carefree, can itself be a danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy-free' reads as one word but splits into the anagram signal and its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or coral near the surface, a well-known danger to shipping.

clue.text: Compass provides spacemen with last gasp help to return

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the whole string is read right to left
last tells us to keep only the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Astronauts at their last gasp are given a compass to help them get home.
explanation.walkthrough: The spacemen are not NASA but NOSA, Norway's space agency. All the pieces are joined then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A diapason is the full range of an instrument or voice, and compass is the musical word for that range.

clue.text: A lot included in cut down first instalment

indicators.note: included in means placed inside, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: to pare is to trim or reduce
a ton, as in 'tons of', is a lot

explanation.surface: A lot of material was cut from the opening episode.
explanation.definitionFit: Part one is the opening section of a serial, i.e. its first instalment: a direct equivalent.

clue.text: Judge fashionable new leader of realm

indicators.note: a new leader replaces the old one, so the opening letter of the following word is swapped out

explanation.surface: Assessing a stylish new ruler of the kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: U replaces the E at the head of EMPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire officiates and rules on disputes in a game, so acts as a judge: a synonym.

clue.text: Bottle emptied before party becomes thrash

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the Labour Party, a British political party

explanation.surface: A bottle finished off before the party, and the evening turns into a wild bash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just orders the pieces. 'Thrash' plays on its slang sense of party.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour is to beat or attack soundly, and thrash means to beat: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cutting bone with zinc is ordinarily involved

indicators.note: involved means enclosed or wrapped up, so the answer lies inside the run of words

parts.note: spans the end of zinc, all of is, and the start of ordinarily

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding note that zinc is normally present in bone being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: A tooth is not strictly a bone, but the definition is fair loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is a front tooth used for biting and slicing, a cutting tooth.

indicators.note: working implies the letters are being worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A working horse was sold off for little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went cheap' looks like a sale, but 'went' is fodder; 'cheap' alone defines. Twopenny is the old British two-pence price.
explanation.definitionFit: Something twopenny costs only two old pence, hence trifling or worthless: a slightly dated synonym.

clue.text: Consider odd boot protection in the garden

parts.note: to gaze at is to look at, consider

indicators.note: odd picks the letters in odd-numbered places, the first and third

parts.note: letters one and three of boot

explanation.surface: Think about an unusual boot to protect plants in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd boot' looks like a mismatched shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a roofed open structure in a garden, giving shelter from sun or rain.

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, roast

explanation.surface: A cold roast as hard as stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold roast' suggests leftover meat; roast here is the verb to slate.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan or stony face shows no emotion: an expressionless synonym.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a brand of lock and its key
second meaning: the Ivy League college in Connecticut

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the secret of getting into university.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is a trademark for cylinder locks and their keys, and also a famous American university.

clue.text: First tie handle in a knot

indicators.note: something in a knot is tangled, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: Instructions for tying something: first knot the handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the lead means ahead of everyone else, i.e. placed first in a race.

clue.text: Many misplay tuba and horn finale

indicators.note: to misplay is to play wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order
a finale is the ending, so only the closing letter of the instrument word is used

explanation.surface: Plenty of musicians fluff the tuba part and the closing horn passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, existing in large quantity, so close to many in sense.

explanation.surface: Left speechless at a cartoon drawn at the funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' suggests a funfair caricaturist; it means fair-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: The dumb blonde is a stereotype of a pretty but foolish fair-haired woman, a caricature figure.

indicators.note: a report is something spoken and heard, so the name is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: Reporting a man stuck in a crane.
explanation.walkthrough: Any man's name could do; the definition narrows it to Derek.
explanation.definitionFit: A derrick is a lifting crane with a boom, the kind used on oil rigs and in docks.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a state of agitation or trouble
second meaning: a jumbled mixture, a hotchpotch

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look culinary, but 'pickle' is the predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew or in a pickle is to be in a mess or difficulty, and a stew is also a medley.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to the West, not the East
second meaning: a cowboy film, of which the Italian-made spaghetti kind is one

explanation.walkthrough: Spaghetti looks like Italian food; it is the cowboy-film genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Western is the opposite of eastern or oriental, and a spaghetti western is a cowboy movie made in Italy.

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of the word attached are kept

parts.note: the middle two letters of strong
Coco the Clown, a famous circus clown

explanation.surface: A garish, brave-hearted circus clown.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a famous British circus performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the florid eighteenth-century decorative style, so the word means over-ornate or flashy.

clue.text: Order member's home to be covered with rubbish

indicators.note: covered with means wrapped in, so the first word sits inside the second

explanation.surface: A monk's home will be buried under rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order member' suggests a monk or nun; the order is the zoological Rodentia.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodents form the order Rodentia in biological classification, so any rodent is a member of that order.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a low wheeled platform for moving heavy loads or cameras

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a toy lorry. The puzzle's theme is Dolly Parton.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolly is a child's word for a doll, and also a small wheeled trolley for shifting loads.

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

explanation.surface: Former drivers who went missing in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagoners drove horse-drawn wagons, an occupation of the past, hence old drivers.

indicators.note: overtures are openings, so each word contributes just its first letter

parts.note: first letters of all and new

explanation.surface: The lead dancer enjoys entirely fresh introductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal dancer' looks like a ballet term, but only 'Principal' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is the head of a college or faculty, so a principal in the academic sense.

clue.text: Unlucky to be poorly celebrated on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the spelling may differ from what is said

explanation.surface: It is bad luck to receive a poor reception on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-fated means doomed or destined for misfortune, a near synonym of unlucky.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a woman's first name
second meaning: a hit song by Dolly (Parton), the answer to 24-down

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a woman struck by a toy truck; 'hit' is a chart success and 24 is Dolly.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolene is a girl's name, and Dolly Parton's 1973 song of that title was one of her biggest hits.

indicators.note: after says which piece comes second, so the pitch word follows the openers

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch prepared after the opening batsmen have done their groundwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central supporting stone of an arch, and figuratively the basis on which something rests.

parts.note: surface reading: a lotion protecting skin from the sun
setter's reading: the sun described as a shining yellow sphere, also a prize for screen acting

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'sunscreen' into sun and screen: one phrase describes the sun and is also a Hollywood film and TV award.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun is a gleaming yellow orb, and the Hollywood Foreign Press award for film and television bears the same name.
